docs.title: Python examples for FontLab
docs.text:
These examples show PythonQt patterns used inside FontLab: owned windows, signals, item models, drawing and small font operations.

This checkout is being reorganized. The previous example catalogue and its source files are archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2. Their recorded native results describe those earlier implementations. Building this documentation does not rerun them or install the previous launcher.

Start with the example collections, then read a complete insight example. For current menu tools, use Scriptmix. For the native APIs, use the FontLab Python reference.

Browse current menu sources. These files and the retained catalogue have separate identities and acceptance histories. A documentation build does not rerun or qualify any native example.

Browse the 100 current practical scripts for current font inspection, proofs, editing, panels and packaged GetGo lessons. Archived dispatchers have been removed from the active Scripts tree. Their original sources and resources remain in the external rescue archive; removing a menu does not qualify or complete its workflow.

Explore both component dependency graph profiles, with complete original elastic controls and an immutable font snapshot.

docs.text:
Use FontLab's existing QApplication and PythonQt.QtGui. Do not create another application or load PyQt or PySide binaries into FontLab. Read the whole example and its imports before you run it. The previous fontlab_python_examples launcher is archived; the current checkout does not install that package.

docs.title: Build and edit the documentation
docs.text:
The source configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. Authored pages are in src_docs/md. The build writes the static site to docs.

./build.sh
./build.sh --offline
./build.sh --serve

The first build needs network access to install the packages pinned in src_docs/requirements.txt. Use --offline after those packages are cached. The build needs Python 3.12 or later and uv. It does not start FontLab or execute the scripts shown on a page.

Serve starts a local preview. Live Edit is available only in that preview; it saves changes to the authored Markdown. The static site has no editing server. Edit generated catalogue pages through their source generator, because the next build replaces them.

docs.title: Include source and shared text
docs.text: Keep usage and setup in the script docstring. The generator publishes descriptions, exact hashes and immutable source links; it keeps implementation snapshots outside the public site. Use mkdocstrings with Python inspection disabled when documenting an importable module. Menu scripts and archived host scripts are displayed as source instead.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
Name the action and its scope. Give one instruction per step where possible. Put prerequisites before the action. Keep exact API identifiers and interface labels. State a host limitation beside the operation that it affects. This is ASD-STE100-inspired writing; it is not a claim of controlled-language certification.

Use page tags and categories to connect related tasks. The navigation follows .nav.yml. Use the print page for a combined printable copy.

docs.title: Echopy native signatures and owned helpers
docs.text: Two runnable examples show how to read what Echopy declares for FontLab's native classes, and how to add a helper of your own without replacing anything FontLab ships. Both live in examples/echopy/ and run inside FontLab 9 with fontlab_echopy installed.

docs.title: Read a signature, or say there is none
docs.text:
FontLab's native classes are builtin types. inspect.signature raises ValueError for their constructors, so the example catches that and prints the conservative (*args, **kwargs) form. Look in the shipped .pyi declarations for the real parameters. The example never guesses.

import inspect

UNAVAILABLE = "(*args, **kwargs)  # no runtime signature; see the shipped .pyi"


def read_signature(target):
    """Return ``(text, known)``; ``known`` is False when Python has no signature."""
    try:
        return str(inspect.signature(target)), True
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return UNAVAILABLE, False


def public_members(cls):
    """Public attribute names a facade class exposes."""
    return sorted(name for name in dir(cls) if not name.startswith("_"))


def report(classes):
    """Map each class name to its constructor signature text and member count."""
    return {cls.__name__: {"constructor": read_signature(cls)[0], "members": len(public_members(cls))} for cls in classes}


def main():
    from echopy import fontlab as fl

    for name, row in report([fl.flNode, fl.flGlyph, fl.flLayer, fl.flPackage]).items():
        print(f"{name}{row['constructor']}  [{row['members']} public members]")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Verified live in FontLab 9: flNode, flGlyph, flLayer and flPackage each print the fallback signature with their public member counts (118, 129, 186 and 229).

docs.title: Own a helper without changing native classes
docs.text:
Echopy never rebinds a native member. install_extensions adds a helper only where the name is free and reports installed, existing or immutable. When a class is immutable, call the helper through get_extension instead.

def call_owned(obj, member, key, *args, specs=None):
    """Call ``obj.member`` when owned or native, else the extension function for ``key``."""
    from fontlab_echopy.extensions import get_extension

    bound = getattr(obj, member, None)
    if callable(bound):
        return bound(*args)
    return get_extension(key, specs)(obj, *args)


def main():
    from echopy import fontlab as fl
    from fontlab_echopy.extensions import install_extensions

    status = install_extensions()
    for key, state in sorted(status.items()):
        print(key, "->", state.split(";")[0])
    glyph = fl.flGlyph()  # a detached empty glyph; native flGlyph() takes no name
    print("layer_names:", call_owned(glyph, "layer_names", "fontlab.flGlyph.layer_names"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Verified live in FontLab 9: flGlyph reports immutable for has_layer and layer_names, so the helper is reached through get_extension, and a detached empty glyph returns an empty layer list. flGlyph() takes no name.

docs.title: Component dependency graphs
docs.text:
Open either graph from Tools. Both capture every current-master glyph in font order; missing bases follow in first-reference order. Repeated references and cycles remain visible. Hover a node for its exact glyph name; the report retains each directed glyph → base occurrence and isolated glyph. No font writer runs. Refresh after font or master changes; a failed capture clears stale graph data.

The regular graph retains part2's600×500 scene,30ms timer,170/distance repulsion, 0.015 springs, clipped five-unit force steps,0.2 settling and1.15 zoom strictly between0.1 and5. It has one destination arrow. Arrow keys move the centre node; Space/Return shuffle; Plus/Equal/Minus and wheel zoom.

Degree Forces retains part3's400×400 scene,40ms basic timer,degree-weighted springs,150/(2×distance²) repulsion,0.1 per-axis settling,ten-unit margins,0.8 initial zoom,custom gradient nodes and two arrows,scene shadows/instructions, caching and mouse/view-centred anchors. Space/Enter shuffle with integer coordinates; Plus/Minus zoom1.2 and wheel uses inverse exponential scaling, limited to0.07..100. Double arrows are the original visual policy; the textual report records the directed component relationship without ambiguity.

Choose Original Nine-node Graph to exercise each complete fixed example. Stop Motion stops the local simulation; drag/shuffle alter only local coordinates. The held node stays fixed during physics. Finish a drag before Refresh or Close. Large captures/construction/force steps have deadlines: an overrun stops motion or rejects the entire snapshot; no subset is silently presented as complete.

Both exact original identities and source hashes remain in menu-adaptations.json and rescue-index.json. Both menus display local graph simulations without writing font data.

docs.title: Glyph Character Map
docs.text:
Open a FontLab font and run Widgets → Glyph Character Map or Glyph Character Map - Styles. Both retain their complete original character picker. The grid shows an installed Reference Font. It does not render the current FontLab document's unsaved outlines.

Each cell's small corner square reports the captured FontLab font: filled blue means covered, hollow means missing. Hover to see every matching glyph name. The proof below the grid lists each text occurrence and its matching glyphs or MISSING. Duplicate Unicode assignments, multiply encoded and unencoded glyphs remain represented. The grid covers the BMP; pasted non-BMP proof text is still checked against the full FontLab Unicode map. Missing coverage does not prevent an otherwise valid original character selection.

The basic profile has Regular/Bold/Italic styles and a 6–72 size spin box, initially 14. It appends at the end on any valid mouse-button click and requires reference-font membership. The Styles profile keeps the original database style/size lists, activated-only family/style changes, editable size Return behaviour, red last-cell highlight and native cursor/selection insertion. Its size list is established at opening, as in the original; changing family updates styles without rebuilding that size list. Font merging retains its own rules.

The basic Copy button writes Clipboard; Styles writes Clipboard then Selection, subject to the platform's Selection support. Verification uses isolated sinks. Isolated surrogate cells cannot be inserted or copied as characters; the Styles profile explains this original-bug correction instead of substituting text.

Refresh FontLab coverage atomically rereads the complete current font. It preserves proof text and reference-font controls; failed or changing reads clear old coverage. No font, preference, history or Output writer is used. Close, Escape and replacement release owned signals and widgets.

Use App>=0.2.103.dev0 through Fly on FontLab 9 with Python 3.11.

docs.title: Glyph Name Pattern Lab
docs.text:
Author a Qt 5 pattern and inspect its captures against the current font's complete glyph-name vocabulary. Use the results to prepare rules for another naming or filtering tool. The laboratory edits local drafts. It applies no font changes.

Use FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.76.dev0. Install matching prerequisites yourself. The complete current source imports its owned App panel through Fly only when it runs.

docs.title: Author and test a rule
docs.text:
1. Choose Tools > Glyph Name Pattern Lab from Scripts.
  2. Edit Pattern or Test text. Both fields are editable native combo boxes. Return retains the current entry in that panel's history. Closing the panel discards these local histories.
  3. Choose Regular expression, Regular expression 2, Wildcard or Fixed string. Toggle Case sensitive and Minimal match independently.
  4. Read the escaped pattern, position, matched length and every captured group. Each edit updates the complete result immediately. Group zero is the match.
  5. Press Refresh Glyph Names to capture all names in font order. Choose a captured name from the adjacent list to put it into Test text. The pattern stays intact. Every matching glyph has its own match position, length and complete captures in glyph_matches.

The retained initial pattern is (s\w+); its test text is small stones. Both checkboxes start off and the first regular-expression syntax is selected. In that configuration, the match starts at0, has length5 and captures small. For glyph-name rules, try ^([A-Za-z]+)\.(.+)$ in regular-expression mode. A.alt captures A.alt, A and alt. Fixed string treats pattern punctuation literally. A malformed pattern has valid: false and Qt's native error text; missing matches have position/length-1 and no captures, with no stale groups.

The escaped field is the JSON-quoted pattern literal. The surrounding report is also JSON, so its representation quotes that literal again. Normal text selection and manual copy are available. There is no automatic clipboard or Output action.

docs.title: Preserve the native semantics
docs.text:
All matching uses the host's QRegExp, including the two different regular- expression modes, wildcard behavior, case folding and minimal matching. Qt's reported positions and lengths are UTF-16 code-unit counts. A supplementary Unicode character before a match occupies two such units. No Python re or QRegularExpression substitute is used.

The original controls and outputs follow Qt 5 QRegExp and native editable combo-box histories. The standalone Qt 5 rehearsal is separate from actual FontLab PythonQt acceptance.

docs.title: Refresh and close
docs.text:
Refresh replaces the entire captured vocabulary. It keeps both authored texts, syntax and checkboxes. A missing font, changed context, incomplete capture, rendering failure or expired traversal clears stale font choices and reports the failure. The local pattern/input workflow remains usable without a font. Capture and evaluation share a two-second deadline. A Python deadline cannot preempt a blocking native getter or regular-expression call.

Close fences queued slots, disconnects only the panel's own callbacks and releases captured names and results. A failed disconnect retains the exact owner and refuses destruction so Close can be retried. Parent destruction releases the remaining owners without dereferencing destroyed widgets.

docs.title: Preview spacing offsets
docs.text:
Open a font, select glyph layers and run Widgets > Glyph Spacing Offset or Glyph Spacing Offset - Stacked with matching Fly and App0.2.95.dev0. The result lists every captured occurrence, including repeated editor slots. Moving ink by an offset increases the geometric left margin and decreases the right margin while preserving advance. This is a local comparison; no font is edited.

Both tools keep minimum/maximum/value editors from−100 to100, initially0/20/5, a slider, scrollbar and dial, orientation and appearance/key inversion. Native arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End, dragging and wheel actions remain available. The three-control tool clamps the value editor and raises maximum to minimum. Its initial controls now match the Horizontal label (the original wrongly started vertical). The stacked tool keeps two complete fixed-orientation groups, StrongFocus, ticks and native cyclic feedback. Its range editors remain independent, and choosing an orientation activates the corresponding group. Native feedback can leave its numeric editor beyond a slider already at its bound; the preview always names the actual slider offset. Scrollbars initially use their native inverted-key default; toggling the checkbox applies one setting to every control, as in the originals.

Refresh Selection replaces all facts and preserves your drafts; capture failure clears old results. Close, Escape and parent destruction release only owned widgets and connections. Empty/sticker-only layers with no geometric bounds show unavailable margins while retaining their advance. Bounds are geometric, not slanted metrics or spacing-key evaluation.

docs.title: Glyph spacing worksheets
docs.text:
Compare four spacing recipes with the selected glyph-layer advances. The worksheet shows candidates. It does not apply them to a font.

Use FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and fontlab-fontlabapp>=0.2.70.dev0 artifacts. Install prerequisites yourself in your intended environment. These scripts never install packages.

docs.title: Open and edit
docs.text:
1. Select glyphs in a Font window, or glyph-layer occurrences in a Glyph window.
  2. Choose Tools > Glyph Spacing Worksheet or Tools > Glyph Spacing Worksheet - Frameless from Scripts.
  3. Edit any of the eight table cells. A is an increment in font units. B is its repeat count. Each of the four rows computes A × B.
  4. Read the selectable report. Each captured occurrence has its baseline and four baseline-plus-increment candidates. Repeated glyphs and mixed layers remain separate, in captured order.

The initial rows are (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) and (4, 8). They give increments 2, 8, 18 and 32. For a baseline of 500.5, the candidates are 502.5, 508.5, 518.5 and 532.5. Zero is valid. The largest recipe is 100 × 100.

Both tables keep normal Qt selection, headers, grid, editing and stepping. On macOS, Return starts cell editing. Double-click also starts editing. Return commits; Tab and Backtab commit and move; Escape cancels pending text. Focus-out, arrow keys, spin buttons, wheel and modifier stepping use the native Qt behavior. Invalid, empty and out-of-range text uses Qt validation/correction. No custom numeric parser is installed.

docs.title: Keep the distinct original profiles
docs.text:
Policy Glyph Spacing Worksheet Frameless Original caption Numeric cell delegate Spin Box Delegate Initial cell storage Strings Integers Horizontal labels Factor A / Factor B Native numeric labels Editor frame Native framed default False Initial outer size 640 × 460 Native layout sizing Editor initialization Retained model, integer conversion Index's own model

Committing a part2 cell changes that cell to an integer. Reset restores its original string type. The frameless profile keeps integers throughout. Both use one real QStyledItemDelegate, a native QStandardItemModel and transient QSpinBox editors with inclusive range 0 to 100.

docs.title: Refresh, reset and close
docs.text:
Refresh Selection commits acceptable pending input through the same delegate, then stages the complete capture. It keeps the factors and current cell. A changed context, missing font, empty selection or deadline failure keeps the previous capture and gives a stale/error status. An unacceptable pending editor refuses refresh and remains available to finish or cancel.

Reset Factors discards pending editor text and restores the eight original values and types. It keeps the captured context. It does not reread the font.

Close cancels pending input and releases the owned widgets and signals. If an owned signal cannot disconnect, Close refuses destruction and can be retried. Return does not activate Close or Reset as a default button.

The complete table works without a font. The report explains that no selection has been captured. No automatic clipboard, file, Output, preference, selection, master, metrics or history writer is used. No values persist between launches.

docs.title: Source and qualification
docs.text:
The framed source and frameless source pages include the complete actual menu bodies. Each facade imports its App entry through Fly inside main(). No archived source or source-relative helper runs.

The independent implementation follows the original behavior contracts for rescued/part2/ports/itemviews/pyqt-official/spinboxdelegate-ddb20b1b68b18a91.py (SHA256 539bd9a3542e02bafe8b89fc847c9b88277859b4e1edb9ac6624eeb7c18a7025) and the same filename below rescued/part3/pyqt-official-ports/ports/itemviews/pyqt-official/ (SHA256 3de6b2d062d29b0721bd8491772ca89bedc4dbe22680ca2af4f333ea6cfd2084). There are no companion assets. Original bytes are archived outside this repository.

The author supplies these first-party samples under Apache-2.0. NOTICE preserves the complete Riverbank 2017/Nokia 2010 BSD header and the collection GPL metadata discrepancy. The implementation does not bundle original bodies or helpers.

The selected-layer getter can call findLayer, which may complete an import. A read-only width getter alone does not prove complete capture preservation.

docs.title: Glyph metrics and revision worksheets
docs.text:
Widgets > Glyph Metrics and Revisions and its Detailed companion keep the two complete retained spinbox profiles. Select glyph layers in FontLab, then open a worksheet. Integer and decimal offsets are independent recipes in font units; decimal scaling applies after its offset. The 12pt point-width estimate uses captured UPM and integer zoom, without kerning or shaping. Prices estimate a proof quote per distinct selected glyph, rather than per repeated layer.

Detailed zero zoom means Automatic: fit absolute total advance to500pt. Detailed zero decimal scale means No scaling. The basic profile keeps literal zero and negative scales. Change precision to round all three decimal inputs, just as in the retained source. All estimates remain local.

The date and time cutoffs independently count whole-font glyph revisions on or before the chosen date/time. The instant counts strictly earlier revisions, including milliseconds. Unknown dates are counted separately. Dates use Qt local time. Detailed retains its historical2005–2010 date range,09:00–16:30 time range and format-dependent historical instant ranges. These controls are useful for an archive revision audit; no font date is changed. Hidden date sections of time-only instant formats remain present and the full cutoff is shown.

Refresh replaces the complete capture while keeping all local controls. Failed capture clears stale results. Both panels are nonmodal; Close/Escape releases owned callbacks. Reopening replaces only the matching profile. Use Python3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.90.dev0.

docs.title: Node Slope And Handles
docs.text:
Set selected node slopes and cubic handle lengths in a non-modal panel.

What: Copy a slope, use each master's italic angle, flip the slope or pivot at the top or bottom selected node. Set cubic handle proportions or Hobby tensions. How: Slope is dx/dy; selected nodes keep y. Each moved on-curve node carries its adjacent unselected handles by the same offset, including at a closed contour's wrap. Selected handles use their own slope targets. Curve modes require both segment endpoints selected. Handle rays stay fixed; Proportions measures length against the endpoint chord. Hobby uses the two endpoint tangent angles and independent positive tensions. Copy Proportions reads exactly one selected cubic. Closing cubics are included; open ends stay. Why: Contour > Align Points and Contour > Handles > Harmonize serve direct edits. This panel adds explicit reusable numbers, two handle tensions and a batch preview. Use: Select nodes, run the tool, choose the mode and inspect the table. Reload selection after changing glyphs. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: Repeat the same numeric rule across selected glyphs and masters. Selection is read separately in each master. Automatic layers, shared outlines, scaled or rotated shapes and quadratic contours are kept. No node is inserted, deleted or retyped. Zero handle rays and zero chords are kept. General node conversion, retraction and Tunni editing remain native or existing tools. The preview lists each changed node's old and planned coordinates. Read-back uses the App comparison epsilon; native coordinate storage remains subject to FontLab's rounding preference.

Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0.

Credit: Independent behaviour rewrite after Vassil Kateliev and Karandash Type Foundry, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. Ideas: node_slope.py and curve.py toolbars. Repository: https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig . No source code copied.

Run Contours > Node Slope And Handles from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Node Table
docs.text:
What: Inspect all own nodes of the current glyph layer and edit X and Y. How: Read node order, coordinates, types and canvas selection. Stage numeric cells in a non-modal table. Apply writes accepted edits through App's outline writer and history.commit. An Apply that changes coordinates is recorded as one Undo step. Why: A complete node table exposes unselected points and keeps refused rows. Usage: Open a glyph. Refresh reads its active layer and discards local cell edits. Table selection selects canvas nodes; Read Canvas Selection reads the other direction without discarding cell edits. Edit X/Y, then press Apply. Refresh caches auto-layer facts; Apply scans them again. Selection reads only the current layer and synchronizes own nodes even when coordinate edits are refused. Selection flags are verified; unsynced rows are named in the status. Benefit: Inspect and edit exact node coordinates without changing node order. Coordinates use each shape's local space. Translated shapes remain editable; components, shared outlines, transformed or locked shapes, locked layers, auto layers and bases of auto composites stay as named kept rows. Invalid numeric cells and nodes changed since Refresh are kept independently. Node types are read-only. Distance and angle columns are outside this table. Window > Panels > Node edits selected canvas points; this table lists every own node and synchronizes its row selection with the canvas.

Independent behaviour-only rewrite of the node-table idea from Outline.py. Credit: Vassil Kateliev and Karandash Type Foundry; kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. No TypeRig code, comments, icons or resources are included. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0.

Run Contours > Node Table from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Designer
docs.text: • Em Star Polygon

docs.title: Em Star Polygon
docs.text:
What: Draw a star polygon in the current FontLab layer as one Undo step. How: Alternate radii in font units, with Y up. Centre the contour on half the active layer advance and half its associated master's FontMetrics cap height. Why: Start ornamental glyphs from repeatable, font-sized construction. Usage: Open a glyph. Set tips, radii in ems and rotation. Generate Preview, then Draw in Current Layer. Each Draw adds one closed contour in a new shape. Auto layers and bases of auto composites are refused. Read-back checks the new contour and verifies every pre-existing shape's geometry. Layers without an associated master are refused. Draw coordinates use whole-unit half-up rounding (ties away from zero); read-back allows 0.5 units on each new-node coordinate. A partial-write error directs you to Edit > Undo. Benefit: Create geometric artwork directly in the active glyph layer.

The read-only shape preview is centred at the origin; drawing placement uses the current advance and cap height. Equal radii produce a regular polygon with twice the tip count. Positive rotation turns counterclockwise. SVG is secondary output for an external vector editor. Generate Preview, then copy the SVG text or Save New SVG to a new absolute .svg path. SVG uses a Y-down em square and contains no font metrics, anchors or hints. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and fontlabapp. Modeless panel. The App panel owns signals and completion. No painter or plugin is needed.

Independent rewrite of the Qt polygonwidget example idea, David Boddie and Trolltech ASA. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. No upstream code or assets copied.

Run Designer > Em Star Polygon from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Glyph Outline SVG
docs.text:
What: Export the current glyph outline as reusable SVG artwork. How: Capture its current-master Qt path, including transformed components. Choose winding or odd-even fill to diagnose counters and overlaps. Why: Keep curves in a vector proof without changing font data. Usage: Open a glyph, Capture, choose a fill rule and Update Proof. Copy SVG or enter a new absolute .svg path and Save SVG. Benefit: Keep rendered artwork for an external vector editor. The frame includes the origin, advance, ascender, descender and ink bounds. One SVG user unit equals one font unit. SVG y increases downward; baseline is y=0.

SVG is a visual proof. It contains no anchors, metrics, hints or raw node flags. Snapshots remain detached. Capture again after changing the current font. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly, fontlabapp and QtSvg.QSvgGenerator. Independent rewrite of the Qt painterpaths, basicdrawing and transformations example ideas (Qt/Nokia, Riverbank). docs.title: Scale With Stem Compensation
docs.text:
What: Scale selected glyphs with independent vertical/horizontal stem compensation. How: Each checked master row supplies two source layers, their measured stems, target stems, scale X/Y and slant. Unslant all nodes, blend X/Y independently, scale and reslant. Preview lists every glyph/master and output layer. Confirm, then Create Layers. The entire batch is recorded as one Undo step. Why: Plain scaling changes stems. Per-master stem measurements make derived small caps or superiors without changing the source masters. Usage: Select glyphs in the Font window. Use Selection, check target master rows, edit their source pairs and measurements, Preview, inspect kept rows, confirm. Benefit: Generate many compensated glyph layers in one repeatable action.

Outputs are new auxiliary layers named master + suffix. Existing outputs are kept. New names cannot contain @ or # or start with |temp|. No in-place overwrite or whole-font default is provided. Preview and Apply each scan dependencies once; control edits never scan fonts. Apply rechecks the displayed plan. All nodes and controls use the same affine blend; TT contours remain quadratic, including consecutive controls and implied on-curves. First-source node names, raw flags and contour names are retained, with selection flags cleared. Advance is first-source advance times scale X. Components, transforms, automatic or locked sources, custom node/contour properties and unsafe automatic dependants are kept. Anchors, guides, hints, element metadata and metrics expressions are not copied. Source layers stay unchanged. Slant defaults to minus the current master's angle; each table row can override it. Extrapolation, boundary-fix, stem probing and saved table presets are not provided. Partial failures direct you to Edit > Undo. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. Non-modal panel.

Independent behaviour rewrite of DeltaMachine.py, Vassil Kateliev / Karandash Type Foundry, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig The small arithmetic helper reuses the Apache-2.0 Stem Blend implementation. No TypeRig code, private identifiers, comments or assets copied. Capture allows 3 seconds plus one second per selected glyph/master. A timeout refuses the whole preview; select fewer glyphs. Read-back allows coordinate changes up to 1e-5 units. Advance is checked against its detached value read immediately after the native setter applies the current rounding preference, with the same tolerance. The coordinate tolerance comes from native source; it is unmeasured in native FontLab execution.

Run Drawing > Scale With Stem Compensation from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Stem Blend
docs.text:
What: Write a stem-compensated blend into a new layer of the current glyph. How: Divide target stems by scale to choose independent X/Y interpolation fractions. Unslant, blend, scale and reslant. The final stems match the typed measurements when the source stems interpolate linearly. Why: Make scaled lettering at a requested stem size without changing masters. Usage: Open a glyph. Choose two source layers. Enter measured source and target stems and scale factors. Build, inspect the output name, then Create Layer. The layer name is Stem x (), for example Stem 75x60 (Light). Names containing @ or #, starting with |temp|, or matching a master name are refused. An existing layer name is refused. Each new layer is recorded as one Undo step through App history. The new layer becomes the active layer. Benefit: Keep native font-unit geometry without an artwork import transform.

The angle starts at minus the current master's italic angle; positive means that the top moves right. Refresh Sources reloads layer choices and the angle. Targets divided by scale must lie between the measured source stems. Equal stems, components, shape transforms and incompatible paths are refused. TrueType off-curves stay quadratic, including implied on-curve midpoints. The new layer keeps the first source's advance. Anchors, hints, node flags and other source metadata are not copied. Automatic-layer owners and bases of automatic composites are kept unchanged and named in the refusal message. Copy SVG is secondary artwork only. SVG import may rescale or reposition it; no SVG import preserves scale by this tool's guarantee. No stored axis setup, extrapolation or batch target baking is provided. Use native Font > Generate Instance for native instance generation. Requires FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App >= 0.2.150.dev0.

Credit: Independent behaviour rewrite of Delta.py and DeltaNew.py by Vassil Kateliev, TypeRig, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No source code, comments, icons or preset formats are copied. Read-back allows coordinate changes up to 1e-5 units. Advance is checked against its detached value read immediately after the native setter applies the current rounding preference, with the same tolerance. The coordinate tolerance comes from native source; it is unmeasured in native FontLab execution.

Run Drawing > Stem Blend from FontLab's Scripts menu.

What: Drop colour swatches onto prefix-matched glyphs to set FontLab marks. How: Capture current-font glyph identities. A drop makes one metadata Undo step through App history. Read-back checks individually coloured layer overrides. Native glyph-to-layer mark propagation is unverified. Why: Organize a review group with visible glyph marks in the Font window. Usage: Enter a glyph-name prefix, Refresh, then drag a swatch onto a tile. Refresh after changing the font or master. None clears the glyph's mark. Benefit: Flag individual glyphs directly without changing the font selection. The table and selection swatches edit the same property; this board adds prefix-scoped, drag-and-drop editing. Glyphs with auto layers are refused. A partial write reports Edit > Undo. Original profile setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and fontlabapp. Modeless; each drop edits one glyph. docs.title: Glyph Proof Layout
docs.text:
What: Compare current-master advance widths and geometric side bearings. How: Read a prefix-matched sample twice and build an anchored spacing strip. Each tile's width is proportional to its advance. Hover for full measurements; zero advances use a vertical marker and a separate measurement label. Why: Compare relative widths at a glance while reviewing spacing in FontLab. Usage: Open a font, enter a prefix with at most twelve matches, set the strip width, then Refresh. Copy Result sends slash names to a Glyph window text bar. Benefit: Spot width outliers without changing outlines or font metrics. Empty layers have no ink margins; their side bearings show an em dash.

docs.title: Glyph Coverage Grid
docs.text:
What: Inspect Unicode coverage as a sixteen-column grid of glyph names. How: Group every captured Unicode assignment into rows of sixteen scalars. Keep all names when several glyphs share a scalar. Leave absent cells blank. Why: A name grid reveals gaps and collisions without substituting font previews. Usage: Open a font and Refresh. Combine each row label with the column digit. Copy or export JSON to record the complete coverage grid. Benefit: Locate duplicate assignments and missing positions during font review. Requires: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App glyph_catalog, draft_signals and qt_properties. Refresh stages results before replacing the visible grid.

docs.title: Apply Unicode Map
docs.text:
What: Add explicit Unicode values to selected glyphs in the current font. How: Paste a JSON object of glyph names and code points. Integers are decimal; strings are hexadecimal, with optional U+ or 0x prefix. A value can be a list. Existing codes stay in place. Why: Font > Generate Unicodes derives values from names. This map also encodes custom names and assigns several explicit values to one glyph. Usage: Select glyphs in the Font window and close Glyph editors. Paste a map, inspect the live table, then Apply Map. Use Selection reloads the glyph scope. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto-layer owners, bases of automatic composites, unknown names and conflicting codes remain as named kept rows. Benefit: Apply a reusable character map without renaming outlines.

Example: {"A": "0041", "space": [32, "00A0"]}. Repeated JSON keys and invalid Unicode scalars are refused. Several map rows cannot claim the same code. Only selected glyphs can change. Typing uses a detached font snapshot. Use Selection reloads it. Apply scans the font once and compares with the displayed preview; native read-back checks every changed list. A partial write directs you to Edit > Undo. JSON is pasted; NAM files and font-library maps are not loaded. Original profile setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. Modeless panel.

Independent behaviour rewrite of TR-EncodeGlyphs.py by Vassil Kateliev, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No TypeRig code, private identifiers, comments or resources are copied.

docs.title: Copy Layers From Font
docs.text:
What: Copy layers from another open font to selected current-font glyphs. How: Map source and destination layer names. Preview and confirm Overwrite, Incoming + suffix, Destination + suffix or Mask. One Copy is recorded as one Undo step in the destination. Both fonts are identified by fgId. Why: Native Paste Special uses the clipboard; this repeats explicit layer maps without switching fonts. The source is read only and glyphs must already exist. Usage: Select destination glyphs in its Font window, choose a source, enter mappings, Preview, inspect kept rows, confirm, then Copy. Benefit: Transfer outlines, anchor positions and advances across many glyphs.

Components, hints, guides, metric expressions, locked/automatic layers and unsafe automatic dependants are kept. Element names, notes and transforms, contour names, node names and raw flags are retained; selection flags clear. Custom node/contour properties are refused. Anchor coordinates use App; existing pin styles stay, new pins use name-derived styles. Anchor expressions, layer metadata, links and colour marks are not copied. Units per em must match. Mask replaces the mapped layer's mask. Destination + suffix refuses master renames; existing suffix names are kept. New names cannot contain @ or # or begin with |temp|, mask, img. or bw.. Capture allows 3 seconds plus one second per selected glyph/mapping; a timeout refuses the whole preview. Apply rechecks the displayed plan. Partial failures direct you to Edit > Undo. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly, App>=0.2.150.dev0. Independent behaviour rewrite of TR-CopyLayers.py, Vassil Kateliev / Karandash Type Foundry, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No upstream code, comments or assets copied. docs.title: Glyph Snapshot Console

What: Evaluate short expressions or statements on detached glyph records. How: Capture once on the UI thread with a glyph-count-scaled deadline and a Scanning label (at most 120 seconds). Choose the query deadline: 5 seconds by default, at most 60 seconds. A Python trace guard stops Python loops and restores the earlier host trace. A loop in native code without Python line events cannot be stopped by this guard. Code that catches every exception can outlive the time limit. Benefit: Experiment with real glyph data and keep complete query results. This runs trusted code in the host process, not a security sandbox. User code can change detached data. The panel itself calls no font writer. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App glyph_catalog/draft_signals/scripting. Independent rewrite of timer-batch and owned-repl. docs.title: Path Problem Report
docs.text:
What: Report contour problems on the current font's current master. How: Inspect each glyph's contours once. List open contours, closed contours with fewer than three on-curve nodes, equal adjacent nodes and small node extents. Why: A combined report gives one repair checklist before overlap removal. Usage: Open a font. Set the minimum extent, then Refresh. Enter an absolute new JSON filename and Export to save the complete captured checklist. Benefit: A build check or another FontLab script can consume the JSON file.

Small extents use node coordinates, including control points, in shape space. They are a diagnostic heuristic, not exact curve bounds. The report does not flatten components. Missing master layers are listed separately. No font data changes. Use Select glyphs with findings after activating the Font window. docs.text:
What: Compare the first captured glyph catalogue with the newest capture. How: Bind both snapshots to the current font package. Match glyph names and compare complete Unicode sets plus modification dates and epoch milliseconds. Report added, removed, re-encoded and modified glyphs in separate change rows. Why: A focused difference is easier to review than two complete inventories. Usage: Run to capture the baseline. Make changes in FontLab, then Capture Latest. The first capture stays fixed. Reset Baseline explicitly starts a new comparison, including after switching fonts. Previous and Next page the display; Copy All Diff copies the complete comparison. Renames appear as a removed and an added glyph. A glyph can be both re-encoded and modified. Unicode order alone is not a change. Benefit: Review the actual effects of a script or manual edit, with every changed Unicode and modification value retained. This tool changes no font data. docs.title: Unicode Issues Dock
docs.text:
What: Find unencoded glyphs and glyphs that share a Unicode in the current font. How: Read the public glyph catalogue. Count owners of each Unicode scalar, then filter and page only the issue rows. Double-click uses App scripting.select_glyphs; its Font-window guard refuses a Glyph window or a changed current font (fl#8528). Why: Keep an actionable Unicode checklist beside the Font window. Usage: Activate the Font window, run this script, and double-click an issue row. Type a name, issue or U+ value to filter. Refresh reads the current font again. If the status line asks for the Font window, click it and double-click the row again. The default dock area is right. show(..., area="left") chooses the left area; top and bottom are also valid. Drag the dock title to float it or dock it again. App widgets.create_panel floats the registered dock automatically when FontLab's macOS multi-window profile hides MainWindow. No separate main window is created. Close or the dock X calls handle.close_owned(): disconnect callbacks first, then OwnedWidget.close() removes the dock and schedules its widget for deletion. Benefit: Select the exact glyph that needs an encoding decision, without changing its Unicode values or geometry. Counts cover every issue, even on other pages. Original profile setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App with widgets, scripting, glyph_catalog, draft_signals and qt_properties. docs.title: Official-demo clean-room work
docs.text:
Owner decision D7 moved the official-demo sources, resources and licence notes to the private fontlabcom/fontlab-python-examples-reference repository, commit 040b2e8, under pyqt-official-ports/. This public tree contains their provenance metadata and 187 behavioural specifications (historical path: clean-room-specs/INDEX.json). All 187 receipts are integrated: 127 implemented, 60 blocked. The replacements and their newly authored resources use Apache-2.0; the catalogue records the spec hash and review basis. All 187 pass native acceptance in FontLab 9.0.9783: the 127 implementations launch, show a populated window and close with every owned object, timer and window gone; the 60 blocked records raise their recorded capability reason without touching the host. Two independent runs agree (workspace evidence examples-cleanroom/final* and examples-cleanroom/controller/). Interactions: 106 implementations had every state control changed and read back without a slot error, then were closed and relaunched; 21 whose specs need files, network, printing, the clipboard or the tray were skipped by reason (examples-cleanroom/interactions-final.jsonl). The 22 implementations without state controls were driven with synthetic mouse, keyboard and drop events on their own widgets (examples-cleanroom/events-final.jsonl): 20 passed; delayedencoding (drag-out only, a system drag loop) and broadcastsender (LAN broadcast) are skipped by reason. The 21 earlier non-official ports retain their recorded acceptance.

Each record preserves its original source repository, revision, path, byte counts, hashes, upstream URL, archive and spec pointers. These identify archived inputs; they do not describe replacement bytes or grant Apache-2.0 to archived resources. sources.json keeps replacement grants in port_license. Historical passes for removed implementations remain historical, as described in the batch notes (historical path: docs/pyqt-official-batch.md).

docs.title: Launch an available example
docs.text:
Put this checkout on FontLab's Python path and install fontlab-fontlabapp in its interpreter (or, for the native driver, keep a sibling fontlab-fontlabapp checkout). Use FontLab's existing PythonQt and QApplication; do not load a second Qt binding or run another application event loop.

import fontlab_python_examples as examples

examples.available()                   # Includes implemented and blocked metadata
handle = examples.launch("QLabel")     # Inside FontLab
handle.widget                         # Direct owned native widget
examples.inspect("QLabel")             # JSON-friendly live state
examples.close("QLabel")               # Owned cleanup; FontLab stays open

The four introductory examples are QLabel, QVBoxLayout, Signals and Slots, and Qt Designer. Further implemented numbered examples and QtExamples entries are listed in the catalogue. examples/remopy.py provides an external controller. The numbered-example checks (historical path: docs/second-numbered-batch.md) describe their scope.

docs.title: Recipes for everyday glyph work
docs.text: examples/recipes (historical path: examples/recipes/README.md) holds nine small FontLab 9 scripts, each checked natively on a font it creates and throws away: layer backup, coordinate rounding, contour direction and start points, anchors from bounds, sidebearings from a reference glyph, kerning pairs from text, Tools > Actions on named glyphs (via fontlab-fontlabapp), and two unchanged Glyphs scripts run through fontlab-glyport. They are written from scratch (Apache-2.0); TypeRig and Glyphs scripts were consulted for tool names and behaviour only. Host-free tests: tests/test_recipes.py.

Regenerate current states and the derived inventory without accessing originals:

python3 tools/integrate_cleanroom.py

The tool validates all receipts, target paths, source headers and spec hashes, keeps the immutable source/resource provenance, regenerates sources/INDEX and updates the manifest's source-catalogue hash. Reapplying is deterministic and resets replacement native acceptance to unexecuted. Original-tree acquisition and analysis through tools/inventory.py remain separate from this clean-room integration; they are not required to regenerate the checked-in catalogue.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest -q tests

Tests use owned fixtures and doubles. Every clean-room record has a receipt, import/build or explicit capability check, and public-launcher coverage. The independent batches exercise replacement behavior; obsolete assertions about removed fixtures and Python implementation details have been replaced. Shared helpers, binding regressions and unchanged non-official ports remain covered.

Run the native acceptance driver separately, in a FontLab session without open documents, from the workspace root (it resolves fontlab-remopy from the sibling checkout and imports fontlab-fontlabapp from ../fontlab-fontlabapp/src when FontLab has it not installed):

verification/issue-104/fl-native.sh --lane L6c -- bash -c "cd fontlab-python-examples && \
  uv run --python 3.11 tools/native_cleanroom.py --batch-size 8 --output OUT.jsonl"
# --ids ID ... selects ports; --reset-stale first clears sessions an interrupted run left.

Run it from a clean, committed checkout: the summary records the commit, whether the tree was dirty and whether the revision stayed unchanged, and every receipt hashes the port's whole dependency closure (its files, the ports it loads and the launcher package) before it runs. Derive a proposal from the receipts, review it, then record it. apply refuses the whole proposal and writes nothing unless every receipt shows six successful phase envelopes and clean teardown, the run commit is in this checkout's history and clean, the driver matches that commit, and each closure matches both the run commit and the current files:

python3 tools/record_native.py propose --output PROPOSAL.json OUT*.jsonl
python3 tools/record_native.py apply PROPOSAL.json --commit <examples commit of the run>

tools/integrate_cleanroom.py resets replacement acceptance; run record_native.py again after it.

Batches reuse client connections; every host phase is a separate call with a 3.5-second host budget and a four-second transport deadline. The driver purges stale example modules, verifies this checkout's import, restores sys.path after every call, checks visible top-level content and owned cleanup/deferred native destruction, and verifies blocked launches before host/builder access. It stops if cleanup fails or execution becomes uncertain, records remaining IDs as not run, and never retries a launch after a timeout. Outputs are JSONL plus a sibling .summary.json; choose a new output name for each run.

The driver performs launch/inspect/close only, without screen capture, clipboard, tray notifications or font edits. It does not update catalogue acceptance. Existing native evidence (historical path: verification/catalog-native-evidence.json) includes historical archived-code records; offline tests and this driver implementation do not constitute new native execution or installed-wheel acceptance.

docs.title: Documentation export
docs.text:
tools/docs_export.py turns the catalogue into Markdown for the documentation site: docs-export/index.md (historical path: docs-export/index.md) (counts per category), one page per category with each record's implementation, native status, licence and a launch snippet, the insight examples and the recipe pages, plus docs-export/manifest.json (format fontlab-python-examples.docs-export.v1: inputs and page hashes, counts). docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Production uses fontlab-fontlabapp for guarded font access, selection and owned dialog cleanup, and fontlab-fly for the existing alias route. FontLab supplies PythonQt. No alternate Qt runtime is installed into FontLab.

Hatchling and hatch-vcs build the small distribution and derive versions from Git. Tests use pytest, coverage.py, offscreen PySide6 and FontTools in an external environment. PySide6 is a test dependency only. The historical launcher stays separate and is exercised without copying it into the new distribution.

GetGo reports require App>=0.2.26.dev0 (unreleased candidate API) through Fly. Optional fonttools>=4.59 supplies standard pens and subset export/readback. All 99 GetGo fixture VFJs and original Apache/CC0/OFL license files are packaged.

docs.title: GetGo font lessons
docs.text:
These 13 packaged lessons use real licensed fonts and retain the original algorithms, defaults, font operations and temporary-copy cleanup. The complete 99-font GetGo fixture collection, its original manifest and license texts ship in data beside the Python modules. No rescued directory is needed at runtime. Native acceptance of this packaged adaptation is pending. Historical9783 receipts in historical-native.json describe the old source only.

Install the lessons and the matching Fly/App packages in FontLab9/Python3.11. The reports API requires the unreleased App0.2.26.dev0 candidate or its later release; App0.2.22 lacks it. Pen and export lessons additionally require the fonttools extra. This candidate must be reviewed/released before normal use. Choose a GetGo Fonts menu entry. Twelve dictionary lessons show a detached, nonmodal plain-text JSON report with source links and calculated results. Font Info Mini Tool returns its retained InfoTool, with report/widget/close. Close releases owned callbacks. Running the same entry replaces its own window. The active font and Output panel are not report destinations.

Each native operation opens a SHA-256-verified fixture as an absolute temporary copy and closes only its exact package through fontpr, including partial-open failures. Mutation lessons naming/spacing/batch_transform require a dedicated no-document FontLab session and discard their edits. A failed close retains the temporary directory and raises. Never run these mutations in an owner session. Export paths must be new, use the chosen .ttf/.otf suffix and are retained. Default exports use a newly created temporary directory and report its path.

For scripting, call from fontlab_python_lessons.getgo import launch followed by handle = launch("font_audit"), then handle.close() when done. To consume a dictionary without a window, import an entry module and call its original run(**kwargs). Parameters and defaults are documented below. Errors propagate; there is no silent no-op or alternate algorithm.

docs.title: font_audit
docs.text:
GG Baar (CC0-1.0): metrics, encoding collisions and chosen anchor policy. Source font: https://code.fontlab.com/getgo-fonts/baar/ Original example code: Apache-2.0. Font notices stay with the owned copy.

Expected output and limits: glyph_count equals manifest glyphs (96) metrics.unitsPerEm is positive missing_anchors follows explicit A/H top-anchor policy

docs.title: Provenance and acceptance
docs.text:
Code remains Apache-2.0. Fonts use Apache-2.0, CC0-1.0 and OFL-1.1; retain each original license and copyright. data/manifest.json records upstream revision, paths, links and immutable hashes for all99fonts. lessons/provenance/getgo.json records each source code hash and its packaged destination. Original function bodies and comments are retained except namespace/fixture relocation, the shared report adapter and the new typed menu/registry interface.

Pure tests, faked native objects, real FontTools export/reopen tests and separately installed wheel/sdist checks establish offline behavior and package closure. They do not prove FontLab native geometry/history/UI behavior. All13 packaged runtime manifest rows remain pending until dedicated owned-font native runs verify actual results, cleanup and persistence on the final artifact.

docs.title: PythonQt examples for FontLab 9
docs.text:
Six short scripts, each focused on one PythonQt technique. They are not menu tools: they live outside Scripts/ so the menu catalogue stays unchanged. Copy one into a FontLab Scripts folder to run it. Each file's header says what it shows, how to run it and what it needs (FontLab 9, Fly with App).

FontLab 9 embeds MeVisLab PythonQt on Qt 5. Widgets and item models are in PythonQt.QtGui (no QtWidgets). Properties read as attributes, some as methods, so the examples read them through a small helper. Signals connect with signal.connect(callable), or with obj.connect("signal()", callable).

Script Shows live_glyph_panel.py Modeless tool panel; QTimer watching the current glyph glyph_table_model.py QStandardItemModel, QSortFilterProxyModel, QTableView canvas_overlay_with_menu.py flCanvas.appendPythonPainter; menu QAction with a shortcut via OwnedMenus signals_and_timer.py Three signal styles, single-shot timers, teardown saved_settings.py QSettings in an own namespace, typed defaults, status check batch_with_progress.py QProgressDialog, chunked work on a copy, cancel

None writes to a font. Offline tests (tests/test_pythonqt_examples.py) prove compilation, import without FontLab and the pure logic only. They are not native proof; see CHANGELOG for the native checks still to run.

docs.title: Learn FontLab models, forms and real-font workflows
docs.text: Sixteen Python3.11 menu entries cover current-font Qt models/forms and thirteen GetGo font workflows. The package runs inside FontLab's existing application. It creates no QApplication or second event loop and loads no alternate Qt binding. The distribution is fontlab-python-lessons; import fontlab_python_lessons.

docs.title: Choose a lesson
docs.text:
FontLab menu Result Models > Glyph Name Filter Filter real glyph names by prefix; explicitly select chosen rows. Models > Glyph Metrics Model Read selected names, advances and left sidebearings in font order. Forms > Glyph Metrics Form Load a Designer form; compare a hypothetical advance with a real glyph. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Audit a Real Font Report fixture metrics, encoding collisions and anchor policy. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Arabic Text Coverage Compare a text's Unicode scalars with actual encoding. This does not shape Arabic. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Outline Pens and Intersections Inspect contour bounds, areas, points and boundary intersections. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Name a Disposable Derivative Rename only the owned fixture copy; retain its license. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Kerning and Classes Report Read typed pairs, zero values and native class members. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Masters Axes and Instances Report designspace coordinates without changing the active master. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Compare Master Topology Compare contour/node types across the fixture's masters. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Sidebearings from H Give I the sidebearings of H on the owned copy. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Widen Two Glyphs Scale A/V nodes, anchors and advances on the owned copy. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Export a TTF Geometry Subset Write and reopen a new TrueType geometry subset. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Export an OTF Geometry Subset Write and reopen a new CFF geometry subset. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Font Info Mini Tool Show a detached information snapshot after closing its fixture. GetGo Fonts > GetGo - Compare Two Real Fonts Compare names and widths using each font's own UPM.

The three model/form lessons use the current font. GetGo lessons use packaged fixtures, not the current font. All99licensed fonts, the source manifest and license texts ship beside the GetGo modules. No rescued directory is needed.

docs.title: Install the matched candidate packages
docs.text:
The current candidate requires fontlab-fontlabapp>=0.2.26.dev0 and fontlab-fly>=0.2.1. Older App0.2.22/0.2.23 releases lack the reports API needed by GetGo. App0.2.26.dev0 and Lessons1.0.4.dev0 are unpublished development candidates. Review and native acceptance must precede release or normal use.

Use a matched, reviewed wheel collection. Some FontLab packages are supplied as checkout builds or GitHub artifacts; do not assume a plain PyPI install resolves all dependencies. The verified candidate collection includes App, Lessons, Fly, Echopy, pythonqtside, TypeRig, Fontport and Glyport. Record source revisions and wheel hashes. Install FontTools for pen/export lessons:

uv venv --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none .venv-install-check
uv pip install --python .venv-install-check/bin/python --prerelease=allow wheelhouse/*.whl fonttools
uv pip check --python .venv-install-check/bin/python
.venv-install-check/bin/python -I -c 'import fly, fontlabapp; assert fly.ap is fontlabapp; from fly.ap.proof.reports.model import show_report; from fontlab_python_lessons.getgo import launch'

These commands create a disposable external install check. They do not install into FontLab or launch native panels. Use Python3.11 and the host architecture for FontLab installations. FontLab supplies PythonQt itself; PySide6/PyQt are not runtime requirements and must not be installed as alternate host bindings.

After installing reviewed packages in FontLab's Python environment, find the menu files under that interpreter prefix's share/fontlab-python-lessons/Scripts. Copy Models, Forms and GetGo Fonts into a configured FontLab Scripts folder. Keep the package installed: menus import it and the form loads a packaged .ui file. The checkout's Scripts/ contains the same sixteen entrypoints.

docs.title: Current-font panels
docs.text:
Open a font, then run a Models or Forms entry. Refresh explicitly captures the current font, master and relevant selection/data. No polling or background work runs. Changed font membership/master or displayed metrics refuse stale actions until Refresh. A failed read clears old data and leaves Close usable.

Glyph Name Filter uses case-insensitive prefixes and keeps font order. Apply Prefix changes only the view. Select Chosen Rows changes only Font-window selection after checking every requested name. Empty chosen rows do nothing. There is no current-glyph fallback; legacy selection writers need an active Font window, not merely an open font.

Glyph Metrics Model uses an immutable QAbstractTableModel. Advance and LSB stay numeric, including zero and negative values. An em dash means a missing layer or unavailable outline sidebearing. Empty selection yields an empty table. The panel has no setters, sorting or hidden writes.

Glyph Metrics Form starts with the first selected glyph in font order, otherwise the first glyph. Choose another actual name to inspect current-master data. Preview Difference compares a hypothetical width in plain Python values. There is no Apply button. Geometry, metrics, history and preferences remain unchanged. The input supports three decimals within ±1,000,000,000 units. A missing layer disables Preview; an empty font invents no rows.

All panels use fly.ap.core.scripting native reads, signal ownership, replacement and Close handling. Snapshot records keep detached values, not native glyph wrappers. A missing, corrupt or wrong-type form resource produces a closable error.

docs.title: GetGo workflows
docs.text:
Choose a GetGo Fonts entry. Twelve entries show detached read-only nonmodal JSON snapshots through App. Repeating an entry replaces its owned window. Font Info Mini Tool retains an InfoTool with report, widget and close(); its App window uses the same read-only report UI. The active font and Output panel are not report destinations.

Each entry opens a hash-verified fixture as an absolute temporary copy and closes only that exact package, including operation/partial-open failures. Naming, sidebearing and transform lessons require a dedicated session with no other FontLab documents and discard their edits. A failed close retains the temporary directory and raises. Export lessons retain new output files, omit native hints, features and kerning, and verify reopened geometry/cmap/advances/license data.

See the complete GetGo guide (src/fontlab_python_lessons/getgo/README.md in the source distribution) for all original calls/defaults, fixture licenses, expected values and limitations. To obtain an original dictionary, call an entry module's run(**kwargs). getgo.launch(name, **kwargs) instead runs the entry and returns its report window (or the retained InfoTool for font_info_ui). Keep and close returned UI.

docs.title: Verification and provenance
docs.text:
The v1.0.3 release contains the original three model/form lessons. Its historical FontLab9784 acceptance does not establish acceptance of this expanded package. All thirteen packaged GetGo runtime rows remain pending native acceptance. Historical9783 GetGo receipts describe the earlier source only.

Current tests cover original algorithms/defaults, fake owned-font operations, real FontTools binary write/reopen, all menu routes, fixture hashes and offscreen Qt lifecycle failures. Normal independent wheel/sdist installs establish package closure and installed behavior; they do not prove native FontLab results.

Build with uv build lessons from the repository root. The version comes from hatch-vcs; a source import without distribution metadata reports 0+uninstalled. From lessons/, run the candidate tests with reviewed App sources:

QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 uv run --no-project --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --with PySide6-Essentials --with pytest --with pytest-cov --with fonttools python -m pytest -p pytest_cov --confcutdir candidate_tests/models_candidate -q candidate_tests/models_candidate --cov=src/fontlab_python_lessons --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=80

Set EXAMPLES_APP_SOURCE to the reviewed fontlabapp package directory. Historical root catalogue tests run separately. Source/license hashes are in provenance/models.json, provenance/getgo.json and the packaged fixture manifest. Code is Apache-2.0; fixture fonts retain Apache-2.0, CC0-1.0 and OFL-1.1 notices.

docs.title: Real GetGo fonts, disposable working copies
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Thirteen original Apache-2.0 examples for FontLab 9. Each entry verifies a fixture SHA-256, copies its VFJ to a new temporary directory, opens that copy and closes exactly that package in finally. Copy paths are resolved before opening so macOS /var and /private/var refer to the same owned document. Successful cleanup removes the working directory; failed close retains it. Nothing saves over testdata. Font attribution and licences remain in the fixture manifest.

All modules import outside FontLab. Entry functions need FontLab's fontlab, fontgate objects and fontpr bridge. The pen/export entries additionally need FontTools installed in FontLab's Python 3.11 interpreter. TypeRig and Fontport are not required for these thirteen scripts. Run edits in a dedicated no-document FontLab session through the workspace native runner. Native status: 13/13 passed on 2026-10-16, FontLab 9.0.9783 (workspace receipt: verification/issue-106/evidence/getgo/examples3-all/receipt.json). The receipt covers run(), declared assertions, owned cleanup and unchanged fixtures; host-free tests remain separate.

docs.title: Repository-checkout demos: run inside FontLab
docs.text:
These are repository-checkout demos, not standalone Scripts-folder installations. Keep the checkout (including testdata/getgo) together and put its root on sys.path once, then import an example:

import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/path/to/fontlab-python-examples")
from examples.getgo import font_audit

print(font_audit.run())

Each script also has a MenuTitle and prints its result when executed from the Scripting panel as __main__; keep that root on sys.path for this route too. No script chooses the current font. The UI returns an explicitly owned handle; all other results are dictionaries. Mutation entries enforce the no-document requirement before reading fixtures or creating a working directory and name any open documents in the error. Read-only examples may coexist with other fonts.

docs.title: font_audit — metrics, encoding and anchor policy (native passed; 0.21 s)
docs.text: font_audit.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). Measured: 96 glyphs, 95 encoded scalars, 2048 UPM, and no anchors. The report also covers vertical metrics, unencoded names and Unicode collisions. GG Baar has zero anchors: both counts make that explicit, alongside missing A/H top anchors. The explicit anchor policy demonstrates a check; an absent anchor is not automatically a font defect.

docs.title: unicode_coverage — Arabic sample text (native passed; 0.27 s)
docs.text: unicode_coverage.py uses Zoto Kufi Arabic (Apache-2.0). run(text="مرحبا بالعالم 123") compares native encodings against unique scalars through a Unicode-only reader. Measured: eight covered code points; U+0031/U+0032/U+0033 are missing. U+0627 is covered; no layer/anchor lookup is needed. Encoding coverage does not prove contextual shaping.

docs.title: outline_pens — bounds, direction and complexity (native passed; 0.18 s)
docs.text: outline_pens.py uses GG Hint (Apache-2.0). A/B/O contours pass through FontTools BoundsPen/AreaPen for exact curve bounds and signed areas. Measured A/B/O: 2/3/2 contours, 11/55/42 points; winding labels and FontLab hasIntersPoints boundary-intersection index pairs. Contained counters and self-intersections are outside the pairwise test; this is not filled-region boolean overlap detection or overlap removal. Each native recording converts QPointF operands to tuples before segment-pen validation; open paths require endPath, closed paths closePath. This receipt validates closed native contours; native open-path coverage remains a follow-up.

docs.title: naming — name a disposable derivative (native passed; 0.12 s)
docs.text: naming.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). Measured: assigned family, style, preferred and PostScript names read back; family becomes Scripting Sample, PS name ScriptingSample-Regular. Copyright/licence stay intact. The small policy accepts ASCII letters, digits and spaces and enforces the 63-character PS limit. Changes are discarded on close.

docs.title: kerning_classes — pairs retain their meaning (native passed; 0.19 s)
docs.text: kerning_classes.py uses GG Stroke Chan OFL Italic (OFL-1.1). Measured on the Italic master: default-master pair count, typed pair sides, explicit zero values, class members/modes and dangling member names. The default run(limit=5) returns totals (619 pairs across 79 left sides, 233 classes) and up to five pairs, classes and members per class; run(limit=None) returns complete data. Opaque native modes become text for JSON. No class expansion or OFL font renaming occurs.

docs.title: designspace — axes, masters and instances (native passed; 0.26 s)
docs.text: designspace.py uses GG Cosm (CC0-1.0). Measured: three masters, one wght axis, separate user/design ranges, master and eight export-instance coordinates in axis order. valueWeight reads design coordinates. The selected master stays unchanged; no interpolation is implied.

docs.title: master_compatibility — compare direct-contour topology (native passed; 0.23 s)
docs.text: master_compatibility.py uses GG Plum (CC0-1.0). Measured: A/V/a match across all three masters; reports include closed flags, compatible and missing_layers. Missing layers differ from empty layers. Equal topology does not prove component compatibility, contour correspondence or interpolation quality.

docs.title: spacing — I borrows H's bearings (native passed; 0.11 s)
docs.text: spacing.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). It plans I's shift/new width, moves direct nodes and anchors and reads bearings back. Measured: I's bearings [128, 0], shift 48, new width 416, plus plan and resulting sidebearings. The fixed H/I inputs have direct outlines; only I on the owned font's default master changes. The basic node/anchor move follows the existing sidebearing recipe; this demo adds an owned real input, an RSB-aware plan and bounds from re-read nodes of the straight-line I outline; native cached boundingBox/contourRect remain stale.

docs.title: batch_transform — widen A and V (native passed; 0.11 s)
docs.text: batch_transform.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). run(scale=1.1) preflights both glyphs and scales direct node/anchor x coordinates and advances, retaining y coordinates. Expected: A/V point counts Measured A/V widths: 640 → 704. Readback re-fetches the layer and contours instead of inspecting the wrappers just assigned; anchors and advance widths are checked too. Scaling about x=0 also scales both sidebearings. Only the disposable default master changes; source data stays intact.

docs.title: export_ttf — compile and reopen quadratic outlines (native passed; 0.17 s)
docs.text: export_ttf.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). Native contour pens capture .notdef, space, A, V; the font closes before Cu2QuPen/TTGlyphPen and FontBuilder create a TTF geometry subset. The native pen adapter detaches QPointF coordinates into ordinary tuples for both exports. Measured: verified: true, format: glyf, retained binary path, exact glyph order/cmap/advances/UPM and full licence name record. Reopened bounds must agree within two units for curve conversion and coordinate rounding. Every contour is also measured with AreaPen after binary reopening: TTF signs must reverse the source signs, and CFF signs must match. winding_verified and per-contour winding reports expose those checks without assuming absolute source winding.

docs.title: export_otf — compile and reopen CFF outlines (native passed; 0.11 s)
docs.text: export_otf.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0). T2CharStringPen builds the same subset as CFF OpenType. Measured: verified: true, format: CFF and the same readback checks. Both exports accept run(destination="/absolute/new-sample.otf") (use .ttf for TTF); the default retains a new temporary export directory. Existing files and symlinks are refused. Outputs are named Scripting Sample, with complete CC0 text, copyright and public source URL. These geometry subsets omit native hints, features, kerning, axes and other layers. They demonstrate pen interchange, not FontLab's export profiles.

docs.title: font_info_ui — a tiny PythonQt tool (native passed; 0.15 s)
docs.text: font_info_ui.py uses GG Stroke Chan OFL Italic (OFL-1.1). It closes the font before showing a QtGui QDialog with a plain text QLabel. Measured: GG Stroke Chan OFL, 106 glyphs, 1000 UPM, Italic master. Retain the handle: tool = font_info_ui.run(), inspect tool.report/tool.widget, call tool.close() in finally, then drain deferred deletion events in the native runner. The Scripting-panel __main__ route calls canonical-module show(), which retains font_info_ui.TOOL even when panel globals are discarded; a second launch closes the predecessor. Native acceptance must exercise this route and verify the plain-text enum, visibility and deferred deletion. Cleanup is idempotent. No signals, QApplication or second loop are created.

docs.title: compare_fonts — compare in em units (native passed; 0.31 s)
docs.text: compare_fonts.py uses GG Baar (CC0-1.0) and GG Hint (Apache-2.0). Measured: 96 common glyphs, 274 Hint-only glyphs, none Baar-only; width differences in em units (right minus left), using each font's own UPM. Nested owned contexts close both documents even if opening or inspecting the second fails.

docs.title: Native execution and host-free verification
docs.text:
native_manifest.json lists all entries, fonts, dependencies, observable checks, cleanup and measured native passes from the linked receipt.

PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest -q tests

FontLab's run_python has a fixed 5-second deadline. Never execute a complete run() synchronously through it: file opening, import cold starts and compilation can exceed it. Use the Scripting panel or an event-loop callback outside the request, keeping run_python calls to short setup/enqueue/poll operations. Preserve a detached result/error receipt and poll it; a client timeout is not a native pass.

Manifest expected entries are machine assertions (path plus exactly one of equals, len, contains, gt), executed by _checks.assert_expected(result, row["expected"]). Paths include dictionary keys, list indices and UI handle attributes. UI cleanup is explicitly handle.close. The manifest's native_followups retain save-prompt, metadata-renormalization, refreshed-bounds, segment-pen and Scripting-panel UI checks for the native worker.

Add --with fonttools to uv run and target tests/test_getgo_scripts.py for real pens, binary and winding-tamper checks. No Fontport dependency or legacy scripts.py API remains; the needed master-report helper now lives in designspace.py.
