docs.title: Samples: GUI scripts for FontLab 9
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

106 single-file PythonQt dialogs for everyday font work: anchors, metrics, kerning, outlines, masters, names, guides, font info, features, hinting, cleanup, generators, reports and proofs. Each one works on the current font and offers a master scope where that makes sense; most list what an Apply will change before you press it, and a few (such as mark-colour swatches) apply on click. Report, browser and proof scripts change no font data (some select glyphs, copy to the clipboard or export files). Many glyph-editing tools group their edits into one Undo step, but Undo coverage varies. Seven metrics scripts warn that moved stem hints are not restored, and font-wide data (font info, OpenType features, master settings) is written directly: Italic Angle (Masters) states that Undo does not restore its change. Read each script's notes before applying changes.

Copy any file into FontLab's Scripts folder (for example Scripts/Samples) and run it from the Scripts menu, or open it in the Scripting panel. A script needs only FontLab 9 and its bundled PythonQt; nothing else is installed. Dialogs are modeless, so the Font window stays usable, and every dialog disconnects its signals when closed.

Each script was run in FontLab 9.0.9783 through its menu path on disposable copies of GetGo fonts, with screenshots and before/after reads of the changed glyphs. Edits on glyphs used by automatic composites warn first: FontLab may rebuild those composites' anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore that rebuild.

docs.title: Cleanup (2)
docs.text: Script What it does Remove Empty Auxiliary Layers Delete empty auxiliary layers (no outlines, anchors, guides, note or other data) from the selected glyphs. Select Unreferenced Glyphs List unencoded glyphs that nothing references, and select them in the Font window for review.

docs.title: Font Info (6)
docs.text: Script What it does Bump Font Version Bump the numeric version and version name; optionally append a dated font note. Calculate Vertical Metrics Set hhea, Win (and optionally OS/2 typo) vertical metrics to enclose every glyph, per master. Glyph Order Preview & Export Sort by Unicode, name or Unicode script; export one glyph name per line for the whole font. Master Metrics Table Edit ascender, descender, x-height and cap-height across masters; diagram follows the selected row. Names & Credits Edit family, style, credits and version naming for the current font. Unicode Ranges & Codepage Hints Report OS/2 range bits and complete printable codepage coverage from every glyph encoding; no font changes.

docs.title: Generators (6)
docs.text: Script What it does Outline Effect Turn the selected glyphs into outlined (hollow) letters. Placeholder Glyphs Create empty placeholder glyphs from pasted glyph names or characters, on every master. Shadow Copy Add a shifted copy of the selected glyphs' outlines as a separate shadow element. Small Caps from Capitals Create small-cap glyphs (h.sc, a.sc ...) from the selected capitals, on every master. Superior & Inferior Figures Create superior (.sups) or inferior (.subs) copies of the selected figures, on every master. Tabular Figure Copies Create tabular (.tf) copies of the selected figures, on every master.

docs.title: Guides (6)
docs.text: Script What it does Clear Glyph Guides Remove glyph guides from the selected glyphs by direction and name. Copy Guides Between Masters Copy the glyph guides of one master to the other masters of the selected glyphs. Font Guides Panel Show the font's guides and add one named guide to every master of the selected glyphs. Grid Generator Add a regular grid of named glyph guides: N lines every S units from an origin. Guide List Editor Edit the glyph guides of one glyph as a table: X, Y, angle and name per master. Metric Reference Lines Add named horizontal glyph guides at the font's vertical metrics, plus an offset.

docs.title: Hinting (3)
docs.text: Script What it does Autohint Selected Layers Run FontLab's PostScript autohinter on the selected glyphs, per master. Remove PostScript Hints Remove PostScript stem hints from the selected glyphs, horizontal and/or vertical, per master. Suggest Zones from Overshoots Set PostScript alignment zones from the overshoots of H/O (baseline, caps) and x/o (x-height).

docs.title: Kerning (12)
docs.text: Script What it does Classes Browser Browse kerning classes: their side, members, and every pair that uses them on each master. Compare Masters Line up every kerning pair across all masters and flag the ones that look inconsistent. Copy Between Masters Copy the kerning of one master to other masters, optionally scaled. Exceptions Finder Find kerning exceptions: pairs that override a class pair, and remove the ones you tick. Missing Pairs List the combinations of two glyph groups that no kerning pair covers on a master. Pair Editor Edit every kerning pair that involves one glyph, with one column per master. Pair List Browse every kerning pair of a master: filter, sort by any column, export to CSV. Pairs from Text Type a word, see each adjacent pair's kerning on every master, and set the ones you tick. Remove Small Pairs Delete kerning pairs whose value is smaller than a threshold, on one or all masters. Round Values Round kerning values to a step (5, 10 …) on one or all masters, previewing every change. Scale Values Scale all kerning values by a percentage on one or all masters. Text Preview Set text from the font's outlines with its kerning applied, per master, at any size.

docs.title: Masters (13)
docs.text: Script What it does Back Up Master Layers Copy the master layers of the selected glyphs to named backup layers before risky edits. Compatibility Check Check that every master of each glyph can interpolate: same contours, nodes, anchors, components. Copy Layer Between Masters Copy the outline (and optionally anchors and advance width) from one master to others. Copy Outline to Mask Copy the outline of each selected glyph's master layer into its mask layer, for reference. Glyph Weight Chart Bar chart of the ink area of the selected glyphs in every master. Interpolation Preview Preview a glyph between two masters with a slider, from the masters' own nodes. Italic Angle Read and set the italic angle of every master, with a painted gauge comparing them. Layer Cleanup List the non-master layers of the selected glyphs (masks, backups, others) and delete the ticked ones. Master Switcher A small palette with one button per master: click to make that master current. Masters Overview One table of all masters: axis location, vertical metrics and italic angle. Restore Backup Layer Restore a backup layer (such as "Regular backup") into the master it was taken from. Sync Sidebearings Copy side-bearings from a reference master to the other masters, proportionally or as-is. Width Chart Line chart of the advance widths of the selected glyphs across masters.

docs.title: Metrics (13)
docs.text: Script What it does Alignment Zones Edit the PostScript alignment zones (blue zones) of each master in a table. Centre in Advance Centre the outlines of the selected glyphs in their advance width, optionally with a new width. Copy from Reference Give the selected glyphs the sidebearings or the advance width of a reference glyph. Equalize Sidebearings Make the left and right sidebearings of the selected glyphs equal, on one or all masters. Italic Sidebearings Report and set sidebearings measured along the italic angle, not straight up. Round Advances Round advance widths to a step (2, 5, 10 … units), keeping every outline where it is. Scale Advances Scale the advance widths of the selected glyphs by a percentage, each outline staying centred. Sidebearings Tuner Set, add to or scale the side-bearings of the selected glyphs on one or all masters. Spacing String Preview Render a spacing control string such as HOHnono from the font's own outlines and advances. Tabular Width Give figures (and optionally currency signs) one shared advance width, each outline centred. Vertical Metrics Diagram See and edit ascender, cap height, x-height and descender of every master in one diagram. Width Table Advance widths of the selected glyphs across all masters, sortable, with odd progressions flagged. Zero-Width Marks Set the advance width of combining marks to zero, keeping or re-placing their outlines.

docs.title: Names (12)
docs.text: Script What it does Batch Rename Find and replace in glyph names (plain text or regular expression) with a live preview. Case Pairs Find the upper- or lowercase counterparts of the selected glyphs and select them. Character Info A live panel describing the character of the glyph selected in the Font window. Charset Compare Paste a text or a character set and compare it with the font's encoded characters. Duplicate Unicodes Find code points assigned to more than one glyph and remove them from the extra glyphs. Glyph Finder Type to find glyphs by name, character or code point; Enter selects them in the Font window. Glyph Notes Read and edit the note of the selected glyph, and browse every glyph that has a note. Glyph Tags View, add and remove glyph tags across the selected glyphs. Mark Color Palette Click a colour swatch to mark the selected glyphs with it (or clear the mark). Select by Mark Select glyphs in the Font window by their mark colour. Suffix Tool Add, remove or replace a glyph-name suffix (.ss01, .sc, .alt…) on the selected glyphs. Unicode from Names Assign Unicode code points derived from glyph names, with a preview first.

docs.title: OpenType (6)
docs.text: Script What it does Alternate Glyph Proof Compare a base glyph and its suffixed alternates in each master. Read-only; outlines share one scale per row. Feature Code Inspector Read-only feature source for the whole font. Choose a feature and search its code. Ligature Recipe Finder Find underscore-named glyphs and existing input glyphs. Name-derived recipes do not imply outline components. OpenType Class Browser Browse feature classes and their members. Filter by class name or glyph; font-wide across masters. Suffix Feature Report Suffix inventory across the whole font. Suggestions are naming hints; review the generated code. Suffix Substitution Builder Preview a font-wide suffix substitution. Append to source only; compile and test in the Features panel.

docs.title: Outlines (14)
docs.text: Script What it does Add Extremes Insert on-curve nodes at the horizontal and vertical extremes of curve segments. Contour Order View Show every master of a glyph side by side with numbered contours, start points and directions. Correct Contour Direction Set PostScript contour direction on the selected glyphs and report what changed per master. Delete Duplicate Contours Find contours drawn twice in the same layer and keep only the first copy. Delete Small Contours Remove contours whose area is below a threshold: stray specks left by drawing or tracing. Fix Zero Handles Find curve handles that sit on their own node and clean them up. Node Coordinates Panel A small live panel listing the selected nodes of the current glyph with coordinates. Node Statistics Contours and nodes per glyph and master in one table, with incompatible glyphs flagged. Optimize Start Points Move every contour's start node to its bottom-left on-curve node, consistently across masters. Remove Overlap Remove overlaps on the chosen masters of the selected glyphs, master compatibility checked first. Round Coordinates Round node coordinates of the selected glyphs to a grid, optionally anchors and component offsets. Slant Slant (skew) the selected glyphs by an angle, optionally the font's italic angle. Straighten Short Curves Turn short curve segments whose handles lie on the chord into straight lines. Transform Scale, skew, rotate and move the outlines of the selected glyphs with a live preview.

docs.title: Proofs (4)
docs.text: Script What it does Glyph Grid Show the selected glyphs on every master side by side, drawn from their outlines. Text by Master Render the same text once per master, stacked, to compare weight and width at a glance. Waterfall Render a line of text in a cascade of sizes, drawn straight from the glyph outlines. Word Finder Find real words to proof with: words the font can set, that use the letters you are working on.

docs.title: Reports (8)
docs.text: Script What it does Empty Glyphs List glyphs that have no outlines and no components on some or all masters, and select them. Font Overview A one-screen dashboard of the current font: glyphs, encoding, masters, kerning, composites. Glyph Info Live A live panel for the glyph you are working on: widths, side-bearings, bounds and counts per master. Glyph Table CSV A sortable table of glyphs (name, Unicode, width per master, contours, components) with CSV export. Label Statistics Count glyphs by mark colour and by name suffix (.sc, .ss01, .loclPLK…); click a row to select them. Nodes Near Zones Find on-curve nodes that sit within a few units of a vertical metric but not on it. Open Contours Find open contours on every master and select the glyphs that have them. Unicode Coverage Unicode coverage of the current font, block by block, with progress bars.

docs.title: Utilities (1)
docs.text: Script What it does Batch Glyph Notes Set or append a note on every selected glyph at once.

docs.title: FontLab 9 recipes
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Small scripts for everyday glyph work, each tested in FontLab on a font it creates and throws away. Run a recipe.py from FontLab's Scripting panel or put it in the Scripts folder; every recipe has a run(font_id=None, glyph_names=None, ...) function you can call from your own scripts, and works on the current font and master by default.

Recipe What it does Built on layer_backup Copy master layers to "Regular backup" layers FontLab API round_coordinates Snap nodes, anchors and widths to a grid FontLab API contour_direction PostScript direction, bottom-left start points FontLab API anchors_from_bounds Place "top"/"bottom" anchors from the outline FontLab API sidebearings_from_reference Copy a reference glyph's sidebearings FontLab API kerning_from_text Apply "A V -80" pair lists FontLab kerning tool glyph_actions_batch Tools > Actions on named glyphs fontlab-fontlabapp glyphs_tabular_figures A Glyphs script, unchanged: centre figures in one width fontlab-glyport glyphs_path_report A Glyphs script, unchanged: report path problems fontlab-glyport

Each folder has the script, a README (purpose, API, native check, provenance, licence) and native.py, the FontLab check that _native.py runs:

# from the workspace root, in a FontLab session without open documents
verification/issue-104/fl-native.sh --mutating --lane L6b -- uv run --project fontlab-remopy \
  python fontlab-python-examples/examples/recipes/<name>/native.py [EVIDENCE.json]

Undo. In FontLab 9.0.9783, Edit > Undo after these script edits names the recipe but does not restore the outline (measured: undo_probe.py in the workspace evidence examples-recipes/). Run layer_backup before experimenting.

Menu use. Recipes that change only what you name (round_coordinates, contour_direction, anchors_from_bounds, sidebearings_from_reference, kerning_from_text, glyph_actions_batch, glyphs_tabular_figures) do nothing from the Scripts menu until you fill in the constant at the end of the file (GLYPHS, PAIRS...). The menu route was also run natively: each file, with its constants filled in a temporary copy, executed as a script (__name__ == "__main__") on an owned font; all nine passed the same checks (workspace evidence examples-recipes/menu-*.json).

The TypeRig-inspired recipes reimplement behaviour only: for TypeRig (MPL-2.0) only panel button labels and tooltips were consulted, and no TypeRig code is included. Host-free tests: tests/test_recipes.py.

docs.title: Place top and bottom anchors
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Prepare base glyphs for mark attachment: "top" goes above the horizontal centre of the outline bounds (offset units above the highest point), "bottom" on the baseline at the same x. Existing "top"/"bottom" anchors are moved; any other anchors stay. Glyphs without outlines are skipped.

run(offset=20)
run(glyph_names=["a", "e", "o"], offset=30)

FontLab API. flLayer.boundingBox, flLayer.anchors, flPinPoint(QPointF) with .name, flLayer.addAnchor, writable flPinPoint.point.

Native check (native.py, owned font): "A" gets both anchors, "n" has its misplaced "top" moved while its "ogonek" stays, and an empty "space" is skipped.

Provenance. The kind of task done by the "Add" and "Move" anchor buttons of the TypeRig GUI Anchor panel (typerig-lib/Scripts/TypeRig GUI/Panel/Anchor.py, MPL-2.0). Written from scratch: only the panel's button labels and tooltips were consulted, never its implementation.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Correct contour direction and start points
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Give every closed contour of the current master PostScript direction: outer contours counter-clockwise, counters clockwise (y-up). Nesting decides which is which, so a counter inside a counter turns outward again. Each contour then starts at its lowest, then leftmost on-curve node, which keeps start points compatible across masters.

run()  # all glyphs
run(glyph_names=["O", "Q"])

Orientation and nesting use the actual outline. Nesting is an exact ray-crossing test on the cubic and TrueType quadratic segments (recursive subdivision, not a fixed flattening), so a contour inside a curve's handles but outside the curve is an outer contour, and one hugging the inside of a curve is a counter.

The recipe reads and plans every glyph before its first edit, so an unreadable glyph leaves the font unchanged. Collapsed contours (a single node, or all on-curve nodes at one point) have no direction: they are left alone and listed under skipped in the report.

FontLab API. flContour.reverse() (keeps the first node, reverses the rest), flContour.setStartPoint(index), flNode.isOn(). Orientation is computed from the node positions with the shoelace formula: in this FontLab 9 build flContour.clockwise reported False for a contour that runs clockwise in y-up coordinates, so the recipe doesn't rely on it.

Native check (native.py, owned font): an "O" drawn with both contours wrong ends with a counter-clockwise outer contour and a clockwise counter, both starting bottom-left, with the same points; a correct glyph is left alone.

Provenance. The kind of task done by the clockwise/counter-clockwise and start-point (bottom-left) buttons of the TypeRig GUI Contour panel (typerig-lib/Scripts/TypeRig GUI/Panel/Contour.py, MPL-2.0). Written from scratch: only the panel's button labels and tooltips were consulted, never its implementation.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Batch Tools > Actions on named glyphs
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Run steps from FontLab's Tools > Actions catalogue (Remove Overlap, Add Extremes, Shift...) on a list of glyphs from a script, using the Pythonic tree of fontlab-fontlabapp:

import fontlabapp.core.host as host

dir(host.glyph_actions)  # 72 actions, e.g. remove_overlap
host.glyph_actions.remove_overlap(["X"])  # FontLab's own run_actions
host.actions.search("overlap")  # related menu commands (read-only)

run(glyph_names=["X"], steps=("remove_overlap",)) wraps that and returns FontLab's own result (contour counts before and after) plus the related menu commands. It never triggers a menu command. Needs fontlab-fontlabapp installed in FontLab.

Native check (native.py, owned font): two overlapping squares in "X" become one 8-point contour spanning 0–600; "Y", not named, keeps both squares; the search finds the overlap commands in the menus.

Provenance. Written for this repository on fontlabapp's host.glyph_actions and host.actions (issue 104). FontLab's Tools > Actions catalogue comes from fontpr.list_actions.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Path problem report (a Glyphs script run in FontLab)
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Find outline problems before export: open paths, closed paths with fewer than three on-curve points, repeated consecutive points and tiny paths (narrower or lower than 4 units). Read-only. path_report.py is written as an ordinary Glyphs 3 script (in Glyphs it checks the selected glyphs, or all; its functions were run inside Glyphs 3.5.1 and 4.2 on an in-memory test font); recipe.py runs the same file unchanged in FontLab through glyport (fontlab-glyport).

run()  # every glyph of the current font
run(glyph_names=["a", "b"])["problems"]

What glyport needs and provides here. font.glyphs iteration, glyph.layers[master.id], layer.paths, path.closed, path.nodes with x, y and type. Coordinates FontLab returns as -0.0 are printed as 0. It checks FontLab's current master (Glyphs' selected master inside Glyphs).

Native check (native.py, owned font, glyport commit recorded in the evidence): exactly the three planted problems are reported (a repeated point, a 2 × 2 path, a two-point path) and nothing in a clean "O"; the outlines are unchanged afterwards.

Provenance. Written from scratch for this repository. The behaviour follows the common "path problem finder" scripts for Glyphs, such as those in the public mekkablue Glyphs scripts (https://github.com/mekkablue/Glyphs-Scripts, Paths folder); their code was not read or copied.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Tabular figures (a Glyphs script run in FontLab)
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Give figures one shared advance width and centre each outline in it. tabular_figures.py is written as an ordinary Glyphs 3 script (in Glyphs it would work on the selected glyphs; its functions were run inside Glyphs 3.5.1 and 4.2 on an in-memory test font, including the anchor move). recipe.py runs the same file, unchanged in FontLab through glyport (fontlab-glyport), whose GlyphsApp module is backed by the current FontLab font.

run()  # zero..nine that exist, width 600
run(glyph_names=["one", "seven"], width=620)

Bounds are the real outline extents (cubic and quadratic extrema), not the handles. Layers with components are refused before any change. It works on the current master (FontLab's, or Glyphs' selected master), and an empty glyph list does nothing.

What glyport needs and provides here. font.masters, font.glyphs[name], glyph.layers[master.id], layer.paths/path.nodes with writable node.x, and layer.width. Glyport has no layer.bounds yet, so the script measures the outline from its nodes (which works in Glyphs too). Glyport cannot move anchors yet (GSAnchor.position write is unsupported), so in FontLab, figures with anchors raise glyport's UnsupportedCapability instead of being left half-moved.

Native check (native.py, owned font, glyport commit recorded in the evidence): "one" (100–200 in 350) and "two" (40–540 in 580) end centred in 600 (shifts 150 and 10), "A" is untouched, and the script's own print output comes back.

Provenance. Written from scratch for this repository. The behaviour is the common "tabular figures / centre glyphs in width" task, as in the public mekkablue Glyphs scripts (https://github.com/mekkablue/Glyphs-Scripts, Metrics folder); their code was not read or copied.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Kerning pairs from text
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Paste a pair list, from a proofing session or another tool, and apply it to the current master:

# left right value
A V -80
@O_left T -40

@name is a FontLab kerning class. Values are rounded to whole units (FontLab stores whole units; halves round away from zero, as FontLab does) and the stored values are reported. Unreadable lines (including nan, infinities and values beyond ±32767, the 16-bit range of OpenType kerning) are listed, not guessed at, before anything is applied. glyph_names limits the run to pairs that involve those glyphs.

run(text=open("pairs.txt").read())
run(text=pairs, glyph_names=["A"], master="Bold")

FontLab API. fontpr.call("set_kerning_pair", ...), FontLab's MCP kerning tool from FontLab's own Python.

Native check (native.py, owned font): three pairs, read back with list_kerning_pairs, carry the values −80, −76 (from −75.5) and −60; the bad line is reported.

Provenance. The kind of task done by "Import Kerning" and "Add new pair" in the TypeRig GUI Kerning manager (typerig-lib/Scripts/TypeRig GUI/Manager/Kerning.py, MPL-2.0). Written from scratch: only the manager's menu labels were consulted, never its implementation.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Back up master layers
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Before an experiment (remove overlap, rounding, automatic spacing), keep a copy of each glyph's current master outline in a non-master layer, Regular backup (then Regular backup 2...). The master stays the active layer. Run it before the other recipes: Edit > Undo does not restore script edits in FontLab 9.0.9783 (see the recipes README).

run()  # every glyph of the current font, current master
run(glyph_names=["A", "B"], master="Bold", suffix=" before kerning")

FontLab API. flGlyph.findLayer, flLayer.clone, flGlyph.addLayer, flLayer.setActive, flItems.notifyChangesApplied with the changed layers before their glyphs.

Native check (native.py, owned font): both glyphs get a backup with the master outline, the master stays active, a second run picks Regular backup 2, and editing a master node afterwards leaves the backup unchanged.

Provenance. The kind of task done by the "Duplicate" action of the TypeRig GUI Layer panel (typerig-lib/Scripts/TypeRig GUI/Panel/Layer.py, MPL-2.0). Written from scratch: only the panel's button labels and tooltips were consulted, never its implementation.

docs.title: Round coordinates to grid
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Scaling, interpolation and imports leave fractional coordinates. This snaps every node (on- and off-curve), anchor and advance width of the current master to a grid (grid=1 for whole units, grid=10 for coarse sketches). Halves round away from zero. Run layer_backup first: Edit > Undo does not restore script edits in FontLab 9.0.9783 (see ../README.md).

run()  # all glyphs, whole units
run(glyph_names=["a", "b"], grid=5, anchors=False, width=False)

FontLab API. flLayer.getContours, flContour.nodes(), writable flNode.x/y, flPinPoint.point, flLayer.advanceWidth, flItems.notifyChangesApplied.

Native check (native.py, owned font): fractional nodes, an anchor and the width end on the grid; an already-integer glyph is left alone.

Provenance. Written from scratch for this repository. FontLab's own Contour > Coordinates > Apply Rounding rounds interactively; this recipe scripts the same idea across many glyphs, with anchors and widths.

Licence. Apache-2.0, as the repository.

docs.title: Copy sidebearings from a reference glyph
docs.text:
Retained catalogue

This page comes from the retained catalogue. Its launch instructions and native results describe the earlier tree, archived externally with historical prefix rescued/part2, rather than the current launcher. The documentation build does not rerun these examples.

Purpose. Spacing by analogy: give "I" the sidebearings of "H", or "h m" those of "n". Each target's outline and anchors shift so that its left sidebearing equals the reference's, and its advance width changes so that the right sidebearing matches too. Glyphs without outlines are skipped. Run layer_backup first: Edit > Undo does not restore script edits in FontLab 9.0.9783 (see ../README.md).

run(glyph_names=["I"], reference="H")
run(glyph_names=["h", "m"], reference="n", master="Bold")

FontLab API. flLayer.boundingBox, writable flNode.x, flPinPoint.point, flLayer.advanceWidth. Outlines are moved node by node in each shape's own coordinates; glyphs built from transformed components need FontLab's own metrics tools.

Native check (native.py, owned font): "I" (x 200–300 in 700 units) gets "H"'s 60/60 sidebearings: outline at 60–160, width 220, anchor moved by the same −140; "H" and an empty "space" are unchanged.

Provenance. The kind of task done by "Copy Metrics" (LSB/RSB) in the TypeRig GUI Metrics panel (typerig-lib/Scripts/TypeRig GUI/Panel/Metrics.py, MPL-2.0). Written from scratch: only the panel's button labels and tooltips were consulted, never its implementation.
